text:
jules: Quick q — client is sending model_select: ['gpt-neo-20b','rw-ice-quantized'] + routing hint {region: 'eu', tier: 'premium'}. What's the exact fallback precedence? Do we try next model ID in same region first, or relax region/tier before switching models? Need this for a mobile client compat check.

kevin: We follow model-first by default: 1) try model_select[0] in requested region+tier, 2) same model in other regions (best effort), 3) model_select[1] in requested region+tier, 4) next model in other regions, 5) finally try any compatible model in any region/tier as last resort.

sam: That makes sense. Can we ensure the response includes which model/region/tier actually served the request? Clients need that to decide whether to retry with a different hint. Something like:

```
"served_model": { "id": "rw-ice-quantized", "region": "us-west-2", "tier": "standard" }
```
kevin: Yep — we'll add served_model metadata to the response body (optional), and keep top-level `model` field for backward compat.

omar: Minor question: if client pins region via `route.hint.region`, should the router ever ignore it to honor model order? We have some customers who set region for data residency.

kevin: If `route.hint.force_region=true` we never cross regions. Default `force_region=false` (so we prefer region but may cross if model unavailable). For residency-sensitive customers we recommend `force_region=true` (we also have Private mode for strict isolation).

tia: Can someone add a unit test covering: model-first fallback, region fallback, and force_region behavior? Name it `test_fallback_precedence`. Also pinging @kevin for a quick review on the router PR. I opened a draft PR: #2345.

canary-bot: Canary check: routing fallback smoke passed on prod-canary (3/3) :white_check_mark:

kevin: I'll take the review today. Note one edge: if client sends both `model` and `model_select`, we prefer explicit `model` (single-string) over the list. We should document the precedence in the API docs and add an example in the SDK. Also propose adding header `x-api-contract-version: 2026-03-01` for the new served_model field (backwards safe).

sam: I'll update /docs/api/model-routing.md with the example and tests matrix.

tia: Thanks — assigning PR review to @kevin. If all good, can we roll the change as a canary next week? :thumbsup:

kevin: Yep. Will leave comments on the PR and add the unit test to the router test suite.

jules: Great — that's enough for my compat checklist. Thanks all :clap:
